name: SGL Events
author: sovereigngl

sections.description:
Sovereign Gaming League (SGL) runs tournaments, leagues and ladders for video games, card games, board games, miniatures and sports. This plugin connects your WordPress site to your SGL organization.

  • Show your events on any page with the SGL Events block or the [sgl_events] shortcode (works without WooCommerce).
  • Sell entries through your own checkout. Choose an event and a price, and the plugin creates the product. Buyers enter their SGL ID (or click Use my SGL account to fill it in) and are registered on SGL as soon as the order is paid.
  • Team events too: a team entry, each player’s share, or both. Shares put the player on their team’s roster.
  • New to SGL? Buy anyway. Buyers without an account leave an email; their spot is held and SGL emails them a link to create their account and take it.
  • Always in step: products go out of stock when an event fills, closes or starts, and back in stock when a spot opens.
  • Automation: list new SGL events automatically at your default prices, and refund entries automatically when they can’t be registered.
  • Refunds and cancellations withdraw the entry on SGL (before the event starts).
  • Prizes as store credit: one-use coupons for finishers, sent to the winners on SGL.
  • Order emails and the customer’s order page show their registration, with a link to the event.

The money goes through your own WooCommerce payment methods. SGL never holds it.

External service

This plugin connects to the Sovereign Gaming League service (api.sovereigngl.com and www.sovereigngl.com) to:

  • list your organization’s events and keep products in or out of stock;
  • check the SGL IDs buyers enter on product pages;
  • register buyers when an order is paid, and withdraw them when it’s refunded or cancelled. It sends the order and line numbers and the SGL player and team IDs entered for each entry. For buyers new to SGL it sends the email they gave for their claim link. It never sends names, addresses or payment details;
  • record prize coupon codes so SGL can tell the winners.

SGL can also call your site’s /wp-json/sgl-events/v1/sync address (signed) to say products need updating. See SGL’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (WooCommerce is needed to sell entries).
  2. Go to WooCommerce → SGL Events and click Connect to SGL. Sign in on SGL and choose your organization (you need to be its owner or an admin).
  3. On the Events tab, set a price for an event and click Sell in my store. Or, on Settings, turn on List events automatically.
  4. Add the SGL Events block to a page.
sections.faq:
Where do buyers find their SGL ID?

On their SGL profile, with a Copy button. Or they click Use my SGL account on the product page and sign in.

What happens if an entry can’t be registered?

The order gets a note with the reason, the customer’s order shows it, and your organization is told on SGL. With Refund failed entries on, the entry is refunded automatically.

Can I still take entries on SGL itself?

An event is either sold in your store or takes entry fees on SGL, not both. Teams can register on SGL and pay their entry in your store.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • The SGL Events block and [sgl_events] shortcode can show a calendar: this month with the days that have events, then each day’s events for the next few weeks. Use view=”calendar” and weeks=”1-6″.
  • Show all events, hobby events only (paint nights, workshops, deck building) or tournaments and leagues only, with kind=”all”, “hobby” or “competition”.
  • Hobby events with no sign-up say so and link to their details; they never become WooCommerce products.

1.2.1

  • A paid order that moves to Failed now withdraws its SGL entries, as a cancelled or refunded one does. Payment gateways use Failed for a lost dispute.
  • A paid order going on hold, which gateways use for a new dispute, now tells the organizer on SGL. Its entries stay until the outcome.
  • A retry no longer registers an order that has failed or been cancelled in the meantime.
  • If an order is paid again after its entries were withdrawn, an order note says to register the player again.

1.2.0

  • Security and naming: every form and request checks its nonce and the user’s permission, and all stored data uses the sgl_events prefix (existing products and orders are updated automatically).

1.1.0

  • Events with several phase 1 sub-events (for example qualifiers on different days) get one product per sub-event, each with its own price; buyers are entered in the sub-event they bought.

1.0.0

  • First release.
